purpose: Determine whether early-2020 financial-factor coverage failures originate in source availability or the current financial event-to-daily materialization path.

root_cause.conclusion: The low early-2020 factor_data5 coverage cannot be attributed to wholesale absence of historical financial events. The current DataFetcher financial paths query by ann_date, collapse same ts_code/ann_date records by end_date, make events effective on the announcement date, and forward-fill without an explicit event-version selection or staleness contract. This conflicts with the established PIT availability module, which makes a fundamental event available on the next trading day and expires it after bounded staleness.

required_repair_contract.source_grain: ts_code, report_period(end_date), ann_date, update_flag or stable source revision identifier
required_repair_contract.same_day_selection: deterministically select the latest report_period, then the latest source revision, before expansion
required_repair_contract.staleness: exclude values older than 180 calendar days from their effective date unless an explicitly versioned factor contract specifies another limit
required_repair_contract.materialization: write only to a new derived PIT financial snapshot/table; leave existing YesLab source tables unchanged
required_repair_contract.validation: compare event counts, selected revisions, effective dates, staleness exclusions, monthly cross-sectional coverage, and fresh 2020-2025 fixed-direction RankIC before any admission review

implementation_progress.detail: expand_fundamental_events now orders equal effective dates by latest report_period before source_revision_id. The regression test demonstrates that a later report period wins even when its revision identifier sorts earlier.

retest_2020.label: raw 5-trading-day forward adjusted return
retest_2020.strict_gate: signed mean RankIC > 0.02, absolute ICIR >= 0.50, directional day share >= 0.55
retest_2020.reason: All three repaired factors materially improve finite coverage but fail the fixed 2020 ICIR gate. They do not advance to annual stability, publication, factor-set inclusion, or model inputs.

annual_retest_2020_2024.strict_stability_gate: at least 4 of 5 annual gates pass

action: The derived snapshot fixes the confirmed PIT coverage defect for all eight conditional financial definitions. The 2020-2024 annual audit gives every candidate 0/5 strict annual passes, so keep all eight out of publication and model inputs; no model training is authorized.
